Subject: Post-demo procurement intake: vendor registration, PO vs virtual card

Hi Amy / Dana —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a few procurement questions so we can map the fastest onboarding path. Short answers will help us pick the right route (PO, virtual card, or marketplace).

Summary from our side:
- Goal: Redwood inference for staging/production inference (initial scope: 5 dedicated GPUs, hosted for pilot)
- Initial contract size: anticipated $120k-$200k ARR first 12 months
- Compliance: SOC2 in-scope; Redwood can provide SOC2 report and network diagrams

Procurement and vendor onboarding questions (can you confirm?):
1) Preferred payment method: do you require a Purchase Order with Net-30/45 or do you accept virtual card / credit card for vendor onboarding?
2) Vendor master setup: do you need a W-9 + signed SOW before vendor onboarding? Any vendor portal link for self-registration?
3) Tax / legal: billing entity and remit-to address (for invoice/1099) — will Procurely process via AP or centralized shared services?
4) Marketplace: would you prefer to buy through AWS/GCP marketplace or directly (marketplace often speeds approvals but adds procurement paperwork)?

Attached is a short vendor packet checklist and a draft SOW for your procurement team to review. If you prefer, we can do a 20-minute call with someone from your AP team next week to walk through vendor setup.

Suggested next steps:
- Amy: confirm (1)-(4) and preferred timeline for vendor registration
- Rishi: I will assemble the vendor packet and W-9, and loop legal for minimal redlines to SOW
- Marissa / Karthik: please stand by for the internal Ops tasks (vendor form, tax info, market procurement cadence)

Thanks — aiming to be as flexible as possible on payment method to avoid delaying the pilot start.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Re: Post-demo procurement intake: vendor registration, PO vs virtual card

Thanks Rishi — good summary. A few quick answers from Procurely AP / procurement perspective:

1) Preferred payment method: Our standard is a PO with Net-30 for new vendors. That said, we can do a virtual card (VCard) for pilots under $25k and where vendor registration can be completed quickly. For anything above pilot scale we require a PO and vendor master record.

2) Vendor master setup: yes — we need a completed vendor registration form, W-9, and a signed SOW for a new vendor. We have a self-service vendor portal; I can invite your Ops contact once I have the company remit details.

3) Tax/legal: Billing entity is Procurely Inc (EIN: 12-3456789). Remit-to is Accounts Payable, Procurely Inc, 120 Park Ave, Portland, OR 97205. AP handles invoices; if you submit via the portal that speeds things up.

4) Marketplace: We prefer direct contracting for enterprise tools (to keep custom SLA language), but if the marketplace option shortens time-to-live by >2 weeks we'll consider it for the initial pilot.

Next steps from our side:
- I can open the vendor portal invite once you send the W-9 and remit details.
- If you can accept a VCard for the initial pilot (<= $25k), I will request approvals from Finance today. Otherwise we need PO creation which takes ~7 business days after vendor record is complete.

Happy to take a 20-minute call with your ops/finance folks tomorrow 10:00-10:30 PT to accelerate.

—Amy
Amy Jacobs
Head of Procurement Ops | Procurely Inc
amy@procurely.com | (503) 555-8442
